page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7571 processors. The instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 192 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware-level cryptographic acceleration is present via AES and SHA-NI instruction sets, though modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 are not supported.

Integrated directly into the host hardware, the m5ad.12xlarge includes 1800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show that the instance delivers competitive multi-core throughput and strong cryptographic execution, scoring in the top quartile on PassMark CPU encryption tests. However, the first-generation AMD EPYC architecture exhibits modest per-core performance, landing in the lower percentiles on single-threaded Geekbench, single-core stress-ng tests, and sequential compression tasks.

With its combination of substantial multi-threaded capacity, abundant memory, and fast local NVMe instance storage, this server offers solid operational cost efficiency for scale-out, parallelized enterprise workloads. The configuration is well suited for database operations, caching tiers such as Redis, batch processing, static web serving clusters, and distributed build or compilation environments requiring local scratch disks.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) from AMD EPYC 7571 processors running at 2.2 GHz. The instance features 192 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reflect standard middle-tier multi-threaded compute, caching, and database throughput, paired with strong cryptographic performance via hardware AES and SHA extensions. However, single-core execution speeds rank in the bottom decile due to lower per-thread clock rates and older CPU microarchitecture. With zero GPUs and generous bundled NVMe capacity, the m5ad.12xlarge provides cost-effective density for parallel workloads such as multi-threaded compilation, relational databases, distributed caching, and backend web serving.
